previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of recurrent cellulitis, diastolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and chronic venous insufficiency was readmitted within 12 hours of discharge due to nausea, vomiting, and inability to tolerate oral intake. She had been on oral linezolid for a recent leg infection but stopped due to vomiting. Evaluation revealed no bowel obstruction on abdominal imaging and no infection on blood or urine cultures. Her acute kidney injury, with creatinine peaking at 1.5 mg/dL, was attributed to dehydration and improved with IV fluids. Anxiety was considered a contributing factor to her symptoms. She gradually advanced to a regular diet, continued on linezolid, and had her torsemide dose reduced to 60 mg daily. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to complete her antibiotic course, monitor weight, wrap her legs, and follow up for ongoing care.
